passages.text: ## Rubric execution and semantic limits
passages.review: An intended procedure supplies no empirical effect estimate.

passages.text:
[RULERS, sections 3–4 and appendix A](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.08654v1)
combines locked checklists, extractive evidence checks and a fitted score mapping
for essay and summarization evaluation. Its ablations attribute much of the
reported agreement to distributional calibration using human scores. This
project has no comparable human-scored sample, so those gains do not justify
post-hoc remapping our constructed labels. The checklist design motivates
making prerequisite decisions explicit; it does not establish that an LLM will
classify mathematical concepts correctly. The full paper and appendix prompts
were examined; no implementation or prompt text is copied.
passages.review: Use the linked sources and stated evidence limits for each applicable claim.

passages.text:
Our current exact-excerpt checks establish attribution, not whether the excerpt
supports a criterion. The observed disagreement between a novelty rationale and
its numerical score is a separate semantic failure. V5 rejected incompatible
decisions but exhausted retries on a conventional probability argument. The
[v6 gate](amendments/2026-11-15-declared-novelty-eligibility.md) instead computes
eligibility from the declarations and retains raw scores for inspection. It
cannot independently certify mathematical truth. Fresh development calibration
under the new identity is required before audit; historical outcomes remain fixed.
passages.review: Use the linked sources and stated evidence limits for each applicable claim.

passages.text:
The user's subsequent clarification permits modest credit for a brief valid
connection without a further worked consequence. The
[v7 amendment](amendments/2026-11-15-modest-valid-connections.md) implements that
construct with a capped contribution, preserving raw opinions. Neither the cap
nor an exact quotation settles whether an added relationship lies beyond the
fixed reference. Those semantic decisions still need calibration.
passages.review: Use the linked sources and stated evidence limits for each applicable claim.

passages.text: ## Novelty-specific judge instability
passages.review: An intended procedure supplies no empirical effect estimate.

passages.text:
[Sternlicht et al.](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.02022v1) vary prompts, retrieval,
reasoning and aggregation for research-idea novelty judgments. Their results
depend on the evaluator and on whether ideas are human-authored or generated;
retrieval and extra reasoning provide no uniform repair. The generated pool has
weak novelty labels, with a limited expert check rather than exhaustive human
validation. Some prompt variants also change the stated decision task, so their
differences are not purely wording effects. This study concerns originality
relative to scientific literature, not our finite-reference mathematical rubric
or quantized local models. We infer that passing familiar constructed templates
is insufficient evidence of reliable novelty scoring on policy outputs. The
full paper, methods, results and appendix prompts were examined; no code or
prompt text is imported, and the active v7 calibration remains unchanged.
passages.review: Use the linked sources and stated evidence limits for each applicable claim.

passages.text: ## Decomposing the judgment task
passages.review: An intended procedure supplies no empirical effect estimate.

passages.text:
[DnA-Eval, sections 3–5 and appendices](https://aclanthology.org/2025.coling-main.156.pdf)
separates aspect ratings and external aggregation. Its benchmarks and ablations
motivate testing decomposition; additional calls cost more, and gains vary across
settings. It uses pairwise ratings and sometimes generated aspects and weights.
Our proposed two-call/specialist instruments retain fixed criteria and weights
with pointwise scoring, so this is an adaptation rather than a replication.
Neither its results nor correlated opinions from repeated use of one model
establish local mathematical validity. The full paper and appendices were reviewed;
no code or prompts are copied. The [dated amendment](amendments/2026-11-15-decomposed-judges.md)
specifies the unchanged qualification gates.
passages.review: Use the linked sources and stated evidence limits for each applicable claim.

passages.text: ## False objections under additional verification
passages.review: An intended procedure supplies no empirical effect estimate.

passages.text:
This follow-up review was conducted after specialist activation on 2026-11-15.
It informs interpretation, not a retrospective justification or alteration of the
running protocol. Both papers' main text, methods, results and appendices were read;
no prompts, code, datasets or weights were imported.
passages.review: Use the linked sources and stated evidence limits for each applicable claim.

passages.text:
[Naik et al., sections 3–4 and appendices](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2604.02450v1)
distinguish finding errors from reliably accepting valid proofs. Prompts optimized
for error detection also reject correct proofs. Their final instrument combines
diverse prompts with threshold voting, selected using development/holdout data;
it differs from this project's mandatory mathematical veto. Their Qwen models
are larger than our frozen quantized judge, and the task is proof validity,
not constructive novelty. The study supports investigating false objections
alongside missed errors, but does not qualify our instrument or authorize
averaging away its validity failures. Its reported gains cannot be assumed to
transfer to the present model, token budgets or rubric.
passages.review: Use the linked sources and stated evidence limits for each applicable claim.

passages.text:
[Huang et al., sections 2–3 and appendix A](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.21522v1)
study rejection whenever any verification call finds an error. They report
better error detection but also unwarranted rejections from smaller models.
Some evaluation labels are model-generated; author case reviews should not be
treated as independent certificates. We checked a specific appendix assertion:
Case 6 calls its proof correct despite that proof identifying a union-based
set map with a linear map over the two-element field and treating a fixed full
set as implying singleton neighborhoods.
passages.review: Use the linked sources and stated evidence limits for each applicable claim.

passages.text:
Our counterexample sets every student's neighborhood to the full student set
S. Then f(X)=S for nonempty X and f(empty)=empty. For distinct singleton sets
A and B, f(A symmetric-difference B)=S, whereas
f(A) symmetric-difference f(B)=empty. Also f(S)=S, yet neighborhoods are not
singletons. These refute those proof steps, not the problem's conclusion.
The [exact finite-set check](development/literature-pessimistic-case6-check.json)
records the construction without model inference. This narrow discrepancy is
not a reanalysis of the paper's benchmark or a claim about every author label.
passages.review: Use the linked sources and stated evidence limits for each applicable claim.

passages.text:
The implication for this project is to preserve and inspect concrete alleged
errors, including disagreements with constructed expectations. Neither source
justifies silently relabeling a calibration case, rerunning a failed audit,
or treating a model objection as established mathematical fact.
passages.review: Use the linked sources and stated evidence limits for each applicable claim.

passages.text:
Updated 2026-11-15. The [state-of-the-art review](state-of-the-art-review.md)
contains the claim-by-claim synthesis and source/license audit. This document
organizes the research questions to avoid duplicating that synthesis.
passages.review: No empirical assertion is independently certified by this passage.

passages.text: ## Which mathematical behavior is being optimized?
passages.review: An intended procedure supplies no empirical effect estimate.

passages.text:
The historical motivation is concept formation and generality in
[McLarty's account of Grothendieck](https://ncatlab.org/nlab/files/McLartyRisingSea.pdf).
The closest formal environment found is
[FERMAT](https://arxiv.org/html/2511.14778v1), which represents mathematical
entities and symbolic production rules and studies interestingness functions.
Its formal entities differ from the explanations scored here. The present
project therefore measures supported exposition and recipient transfer, not
discovery of a new mathematical theory.
passages.review: Use the linked sources and stated evidence limits for each applicable claim.

passages.text:
The [novelty/OOD amendment](amendments/2026-11-15-valid-novelty-and-ood.md)
explicitly tests useful departures from documented conventional approaches.
FERMAT's definition/conjecture production and productivity/comprehensibility
measures motivate checking what a construction enables, beyond its name or
unfamiliarity. Its results do not validate our natural-language novelty score;
the calibration and held-out evaluations must establish its local usefulness.
passages.review: Use the linked sources and stated evidence limits for each applicable claim.

passages.text: ## How is behavior selected?
passages.review: An intended procedure supplies no empirical effect estimate.

passages.text:
[DeepSeekMath](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.03300v3) supplies the original GRPO
method; [TRL](https://huggingface.co/docs/trl/grpo_trainer) supplies the maintained
implementation. [Dr. GRPO](https://arxiv.org/html/2503.20783v2) motivates removing
length and within-group standard-deviation normalization.
[Rubrics as Rewards](https://arxiv.org/html/2507.17746v1) is the direct precedent
for decomposed judgment. The additional correctness gate is a project design
choice. The maximum theory bonus and validity rule are hypotheses to test, not
values established by those papers.
passages.review: Use the linked sources and stated evidence limits for each applicable claim.

passages.text: ## What would constitute evidence?
passages.review: An intended procedure supplies no empirical effect estimate.

passages.text:
[Judge evaluation research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.05685) motivates testing
judge behavior rather than assuming it is correct. The protocol separates
training reward, independent-family judgment, and verified recipient accuracy.
These measures can disagree, which is scientifically informative.
passages.review: The cross-family design predates the active same-family experiment.

passages.text:
The observed development confusion between conventional generality and novelty
also motivates examining judgment order. [MT-Bench's published mathematical
judge prompts](https://github.com/lm-sys/FastChat/blob/main/fastchat/llm_judge/data/judge_prompts.jsonl)
request a comparison and explanation before the final rating.
[G-Eval](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2303.16634) instead supplies generated evaluation
steps and combines score probabilities; our implementation does not reproduce
that method. Neither source establishes that changing JSON field order will
repair this project's novelty judgments.
[Yamauchi et al.](https://arxiv.org/html/2506.13639v1) find little additional
benefit from explicit reasoning when detailed criteria and references are
present in their evaluated settings. Their tasks and evaluators differ from
ours. Any reasoning-order or decoding change here therefore needs its own
development experiment and fresh audit, not an assumed reliability improvement.
The [subsequent inference review](judge-inference-review.md) examines native
thinking and small-judge budget studies after the observed v4 failures. It
distinguishes pairwise preference, final-answer judging and our theory rubric.
passages.review: Use the linked sources and stated evidence limits for each applicable claim.

passages.text:
The evaluation structure follows the separation of development and testing
discussed by [Lones](https://arxiv.org/html/2108.02497v4). Claims about a latent
mechanism would require additional evidence of the kind of distinction between
explanation and speculation emphasized by
[Lipton and Steinhardt](https://arxiv.org/html/1807.03341). None is promised here.
passages.review: Use the linked sources and stated evidence limits for each applicable claim.

passages.text: ## Search scope and remaining uncertainty
passages.review: An intended procedure supplies no empirical effect estimate.

passages.text:
The 2026-11-16 smaller-GPU amendment reuses the existing training/inference stack.
[Qwen's 0.8B model card](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B) and the
[2B](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen3.5-2B-GGUF) and
[4B](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen3.5-4B-GGUF) quantized repositories supply
Apache-2.0 model artifacts. [Unsloth's guide](https://unsloth.ai/docs/models/qwen3.5/fine-tune)
supports the smaller policy and recommends its non-vLLM route for GRPO, while

passages.text: ## Abstract
passages.review: An intended procedure supplies no empirical effect estimate.

passages.text: We specify a local experiment testing whether correctness-gated rubric rewards improve useful mathematical theory building. A frozen Qwen judge assesses explanations; external arithmetic verifies final answers. Separate frozen judging and frozen-recipient transfer assess behavior. Qualified-study analysis status: pending. After calibration failures, a user-authorized exploratory continuation uses a single judge call despite unqualified rewards. Its results remain separate. No latent-space mechanism is established.

passages.text: ## Context, motivation and related work
passages.review: An intended procedure supplies no empirical effect estimate.

passages.text: Grothendieck's rising-sea metaphor motivates building structures until a specific question becomes a consequence. McLarty's account supplies the historical attribution [1]. We combine GRPO [2], Dr. GRPO normalization [3], and rubric rewards [4]. FERMAT [5] studies symbolic theory formation; this study instead scores natural-language explanations. The contribution is a correctness-gated experimental protocol and reusable environment, not a new optimizer.

passages.text: ## Method
passages.review: An intended procedure supplies no empirical effect estimate.

passages.text: Tasks come from pinned Reasoning Gym generators [6]. Training families are GCD, LCM, polynomial multiplication and dice probabilities. Semantic deduplication separates train, development, fresh, harder and unseen-family evaluation. One terminal final-answer field is checked by restricted arithmetic and Math-Verify [7]. Correctness C multiplies the entire reward: R=C(1+0.5T). Theory T is a six-criterion rubric score gated by supported validity. Constructive novelty receives 20% weight, judged relative to published conventional approaches. New objects, definitions, invariants, frameworks and distant mathematical connections earn that credit only when justified and useful. Historical originality and pretraining distribution are not inferred. Supporting excerpts are required. The two-call protocol separated conceptual analysis from overall validity and quality. Its historical fallback used eight specialist roles. That protocol derived novelty from explicit addition, application and consequence findings, and withholds novelty unless supported theory is declared beyond-reference with an excerpt identifying a concrete addition. Brief valid connections can earn one novelty point without a further worked use; developed mathematics can earn up to four. A reference argument establishing a connection is not itself a further application. Raw stage findings are retained; code derives combined scores and any substantive objection vetoes the bonus. Checklist-based judging [14] and decomposition [15] motivate auditable prerequisites; the checks do not certify mathematical entailment. Final-answer verification does not certify surrounding proofs.

passages.review: An intended procedure supplies no empirical effect estimate.

passages.text: The active smaller-model experiment selects Qwen3.5-0.8B BF16 LoRA, with a frozen Qwen3.5-2B Q4_K_M training judge resident on the same GPU. A frozen Qwen3.5-4B Q4_K_M evaluator runs on GPU after policy generation. All policy parameters and judge layers must fit on CUDA; tokenization, verification and logging remain CPU work. The earlier 2B-policy/9B-CPU-judge/Gemma-12B setup is postponed and preserved. Exact revisions and dependencies are locked. Unsloth's documented non-vLLM route [8] and TRL [9] implement training. The preregistration fixes group size, optimizer settings, sample budgets and fallback criteria. A pre-comparison runtime-budget amendment selects 64 optimizer updates for every training arm. The deferred qualification protocol is specialists-v1; per-role prompts, visible/reasoning budgets and dependencies are locked in its identity. Separate calls reuse the same frozen model and may share errors. Studies report setting-dependent benefits and failures of additional judging computation [12,13]; neither validates this novelty rubric. Failed feasibility or calibration is development evidence, not a negative test of the behavioral hypothesis.

passages.review: An intended procedure supplies no empirical effect estimate.

passages.text: Preserved development logs contain 270 completed judge responses and 10 requests without a completed response. These counts are generated from reports/development logs. Interrupted CPU and CUDA judging attempts and runtime changes are documented in dated amendments. CUDA loading succeeded, but slow decoding motivated a bounded thread-count diagnostic before recalibration. Partial judgments do not establish calibration reliability. Conventional arguments received nonzero novelty credit, including after the v3 clarification. The clean standalone Gemma retry completed judgments, including a rejected abbreviated quote and an accepted retry. V4 requests evidence before scores and supplies bounded validation feedback. V4 Gemma contrasts favored valid bridges but also assigned novelty to some conventional controls. Passive OpenMP waiting completed the observed requests without a transport failure; that short run does not establish sustained reliability. Qwen's subsequent partial v4 attempt also assigned no-theory verdicts to conventional generalized explanations. It was interrupted for a documented reasoning-mode development revision, without being declared a calibration pass or threshold failure. The later v5 attempt stopped after bounded retries repeated a contradiction between the declared reference relation and numerical novelty score; that calibration remained incomplete. V6 demonstrated a logged eligibility gate on that discrepancy, then was interrupted when the user clarified that brief valid connections should receive modest novelty credit. V7 implements that changed construct. Its first trial failed the control-credit conditions despite correct observed framework/control rankings. A later reference-scope amendment clarified commutative-polynomial and ordinary biased-probability baselines. That trial also failed: routine probability controls received zero novelty, but brief commutator connections remained uncredited and a brief subgroup connection tied a developed framework on novelty while scoring higher overall. A conventional invariant was cited as a use of the added connection; exact-excerpt validation cannot establish that semantic attribution. Historical results are retained, and qualification remains unestablished. The two-call decomposition subsequently failed development: it credited a brief commutator connection but overcredited conventional GCD/LCM mathematics and missed developed uses. The preserved stage findings and case report document these errors. The preregistered specialist fallback also failed quoted-Qwen development. Its roles emitted mathematical objections to omitted elementary steps, conventionality and perceived irrelevance, removing bonuses from valid frameworks and a brief connection. Selected exact checks of the disputed steps are preserved without rescoring the trial. Rubric-only Qwen specialist development also failed: correct validity findings were vetoed by other roles, while a conventional calculation was mistaken for use of a brief connection. Quoted Gemma specialist development was deferred following the user's new execution instruction. Related proof-verification studies discuss false rejection [16,17], but use different models and aggregation rules and do not qualify this instrument.

passages.text: ## Exploratory continuation with a single judge
passages.review: An intended procedure supplies no empirical effect estimate.

passages.text: The dated amendment explicitly permits training without calibration qualification. It retains the latest published single-call rubric v7, fixed references, modest connection credit, weights, correctness gate and training settings. Following an exact-quotation execution failure, a new identity retains context preflight and replaces quotation copying with constrained passage IDs. Code extracts original source text; this follows the general source-location citation idea [19], using only local Qwen/Gemma. After the smaller judge repeatedly exhausted its output budget, a separate identity bounds rationale length and evidence/problem lists in the wire format without changing scoring rules. It does not verify that a selected passage entails the judge's claim. Each correct solution receives one accepted structured assessment; only output or transport failures permit bounded retries. Separate names and checkpoint identities keep these runs out of the qualified study. The initial comparison is theory bonus versus correctness-only at seed 42, with ordinary and rising-sea prompted baselines. The current 4B Qwen evaluator's scores are also unqualified. Both judges share a model family and may share systematic errors. The larger CPU setup was postponed at the user's request after a partial ordinary baseline; its saved outputs are not pooled with the smaller-policy comparison. The model-size change also changes the reward instrument, so historical timing or scores cannot isolate a CPU-versus-GPU effect. Held-out correctness and recipient transfer are therefore particularly useful checks, while judged theory remains a potentially biased proxy. Reward-model overoptimization has been observed in a distinct synthetic reward-model setting [18]; it does not determine this experiment's outcome. All uncertainty remains exploratory even if later seeds or nominal targets agree. Larger, better judges are future experiments requiring new frozen identities and fresh held-out confirmation. Analysis status: pending. No matched trained arms have been evaluated.

passages.text: ## Discussion and limitations
passages.review: An intended procedure supplies no empirical effect estimate.

passages.text: Judge scores are imperfect proxies. The current training and evaluation judges share the Qwen family and may share biases or training data; the cross-family comparison is deferred. Quantization can change judgments. Synthetic elementary tasks limit external validity. The constructed audit changes numerical instances while sharing mathematical templates with development; it does not establish generalization to unseen failure types. Fixed small-seed comparisons may be inconclusive. Reusable exposition is not equivalent to historically novel mathematics. Higher training scores without independent or transfer improvement are consistent with proxy optimization. Do not infer a latent mechanism from behavioral scores alone. Development/test separation and scoped claims follow methodological guidance [10,11].

passages.text: ## Postponed research directions
passages.review: An intended procedure supplies no empirical effect estimate.

passages.text: After the current experiment sequence, the user requests trials with 10B+, 100B+ and 1T+ parameter models, advanced agentic RL, Lean-based formal feedback, and explicit quantitative rewards replacing LLM judging where feasible. These are future research intentions, not implemented methods or results. Candidate measures include token/compute costs, checked consequences, dependency-based reuse and held-out transfer. Exact calculation does not establish that a metric captures conceptual novelty, generality or understanding. docs/future-research.md documents candidate measures, source links and required controls. Each direction needs a new registered protocol; the current small-model experiment and reward remain unchanged. If prespecified development diagnostics find that the small policy cannot solve the current tasks, a separate easier-mathematics experiment is authorized, preserving the present tasks for larger models. Difficulty must not be selected on held-out scores or changed within a comparison. The current pilot contains correct completions, so this fallback is not activated. The dated task-difficulty amendment records the diagnosis and separation requirements.

passages.text: ## Question, hypotheses and falsification
passages.review: Read the dated identity with its contemporaneous records and amendments.

passages.text:
Does a Grothendieck-inspired rubric bonus improve useful mathematical theory
building without materially reducing answer accuracy? The mechanism motivating
this study is behavior selection through RL, not an established latent direction.
The method combines [GRPO](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.03300v3),
[Dr. GRPO normalization](https://arxiv.org/html/2503.20783v2) and
[rubric rewards](https://arxiv.org/html/2507.17746v1).
passages.review: Read the dated identity with its contemporaneous records and amendments.

passages.text:
Primary H1: the proposed arm improves mean correctness-weighted independent
theory score by at least 0.05 over correctness-only GRPO, with a paired two-sided
95% interval whose lower bound exceeds zero. Accuracy must be noninferior:
the lower endpoint of the paired two-sided 95% interval for accuracy difference
must exceed -0.03. All three conditions are required. An interval containing
zero is inconclusive, not confirmation. An upper theory-score endpoint below
0.05 rules out the prespecified useful effect at this precision. Clear accuracy
inferiority contradicts the combined hypothesis.
passages.review: Read the dated identity with its contemporaneous records and amendments.

passages.text:
Secondary H2: reusable notes from the proposed policy improve a frozen
recipient's verified accuracy compared with no notes, unrelated notes, and
baseline notes. This is exploratory and reported with intervals, without a
confirmatory significance claim. Higher training-judge scores without independent
improvement are consistent with proxy optimization. Neither outcome establishes
a latent-space mechanism.
passages.review: Read the dated identity with its contemporaneous records and amendments.

passages.text: ## Data and locked splits
passages.review: Read the dated identity with its contemporaneous records and amendments.

passages.text:
Use pinned Reasoning Gym generators. Train on 1,024 problems, balanced across
GCD, LCM, polynomial multiplication and dice probabilities. Development has 64
balanced problems. The locked primary set has 400 problems: 200 fresh standard
instances (50 per trained family), 100 harder instances (25 per trained family),
and 100 new-family instances (50 prime factorizations, 50 polynomial equations).
passages.review: Read the dated identity with its contemporaneous records and amendments.

passages.text:
Standard GCD: 2–3 integers in 2–1000; LCM: 2–3 in 2–100; polynomial
multiplication: 2 factors, 2–3 terms, degree 0–2, coefficient magnitudes 1–8,
one variable x; dice: 3 dice, maximum size 20. Harder GCD: 4–5 integers in
1001–10000; harder LCM: 4–5 in 101–300; harder products: 3 factors, 3–4 terms,
degree 0–3, magnitudes 1–12; harder dice: 5 dice, maximum size 24.
New-family factorization uses 100–10000; equations use degree 1–3,
2–4 terms, coefficient magnitudes 1–10, all real roots to nearest four decimals.
Generator mistakes or degeneracies are filtered by deterministic checks before
any policy output and logged with reasons; no filtering based on model success.

passages.text: ## Training and arms
passages.review: Read the dated identity with its contemporaneous records and amendments.

passages.text:
LoRA rank 16, alpha 32, dropout 0; language modules only. Four completions per
prompt; per-device microbatch 1; gradient accumulation 8. Learning rate 1e-5,
linear scheduler, warmup ratio 0.1, AdamW, gradient clipping 1, maximum 256
optimizer updates. TRL `dr_grpo`, `scale_rewards=False`, KL coefficient 0.04,
epsilon 0.2, one update per rollout, no vLLM for Qwen3.5. Completion limit 2048,
prompt limit 512, temperature 1, top-p 1. Save at optimizer boundaries at least
every 8 steps and upon orderly termination. Resume state includes adapter,
optimizer, scheduler, RNG, data position, config and durable judge cache.

passages.text: ## Reward and judge calibration
passages.review: Read the dated identity with its contemporaneous records and amendments.

passages.text:
Require exactly one `<final>...</final>` answer. Invalid format and incorrect
answers receive zero. Task-specific checks plus bounded Math-Verify establish C;
parser crashes/timeouts are infrastructure failures with explicit retry/termination.
Only correct responses are sent for theory scoring. T is a weighted mean of
0–4 rubric scores divided by four, and is zero unless theory validity is
`supported`. Nonzero criterion scores require exact supporting response excerpts.
No verbosity, name-dropping or metaphor bonus. Full prompt and schema are versioned.
passages.review: Read the dated identity with its contemporaneous records and amendments.

passages.text:
Weights: structural understanding .25; justified generality .25; problem as
consequence .20; reuse/connections .20; conceptual economy/exposition .10.
Validity states: none, supported, unsupported, contradicted. Invalid judge JSON,
missing evidence or network/service failure triggers bounded retries then a hard
failure; it never silently becomes a mathematical error or a zero-theory label.
passages.review: Read the dated identity with its contemporaneous records and amendments.

passages.text:
Calibrate each exact judge and the rubric-only training-judge variant using
separate constructed development and locked audit cases. Each split contains
20 preference pairs and 20 deliberate false-theory cases, including padding,
irrelevant jargon and embedded grading instructions. Preference order is strict
T(useful explanation)>T(mechanical/padded/wrong-theory explanation); ties fail.
Pass requires at least 80% correct order and at least 90% false-theory bonuses
suppressed, separately for every required judge/prompt configuration. These are
constructed test expectations, not human preference evidence. Development may
inform prompt edits; use locked audit once. Failure blocks long training;
subsequent changes require a dated amendment and newly reserved audit cases.

passages.text: ## Analysis and uncertainty
passages.review: Read the dated identity with its contemporaneous records and amendments.

passages.text:
For each locked problem i and training seed s, save C and independent judge T,
then compute M=C*T. Primary estimate is the mean paired proposed-minus-correctness
difference, first averaged across the three matched seeds within each problem,
then across problems. Report every seed and between-seed sample SD. Use 10000
stratified paired bootstrap resamples of problem IDs (fixed RNG seed 20261115),
retaining all seed outcomes for an ID together and preserving the three stratum
sizes. Report percentile 95% intervals. These intervals are conditional on the
three seeds; a separate hierarchical bootstrap resampling matched seed pairs
and problems is a sensitivity analysis, explicitly weak with only three seeds.
passages.review: Read the dated identity with its contemporaneous records and amendments.

passages.text:
Accuracy noninferiority uses the same paired stratified resampling. Publish
stratum-specific accuracy, M, theory conditional on correctness, length, valid
format rate, failure counts and judge latency as secondary descriptive metrics.
Transfer resamples source IDs, keeping each source's four targets and all
conditions together. No treating generations, seeds or probes as independent
problem samples. No post-hoc exclusions of difficult or unfavorable outputs.
Corrected implementation errors invalidate and rerun affected comparisons with
an amendment. A failed model generation is recorded, not dropped from accuracy.
Infrastructure failures are separately enumerated and retried identically.
passages.review: Read the dated identity with its contemporaneous records and amendments.

passages.text:
The first single-seed result is exploratory and cannot meet the confirmatory
claim. Other arms and subgroup analyses are descriptive; no uncorrected family
of confirmatory tests. Do not increase sample size merely to cross a threshold.
Report all runs, including failed pilots, zero-variance groups and negative results.

passages.review: Read the dated identity with its contemporaneous records and amendments.

passages.text:
Stop on nonfinite losses, repeated infrastructure errors, audit failure, failed
checkpoint recovery or exhausted budget. A wrong answer alone is not an
infrastructure failure. Publish a milestone before each model stage and after
each run/evaluation; do not hide unsuccessful stages. All empirical numbers,
tables and figures are regenerated from saved machine-readable records.

Limitations include subjective and possibly correlated judges, quantization,
small models and synthetic families, uncertain contamination, only three seeds,
and potentially low power at the fixed sample size. No latent-space measurements
are included. See the [review](state-of-the-art-review.md) for primary sources.

passages.review: An intended procedure supplies no empirical effect estimate.

passages.text:
Can a correctness-gated, evidence-bearing rubric reward improve reusable
mathematical explanations and downstream problem solving? The proposed
contribution is an experiment combining existing components, not a new policy
optimizer or a demonstration of mechanistic latent-space steering.

| Source | Relevant finding or design | Reuse and boundary |
|---|---|---|
| [DeepSeekMath, §4](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.03300v3) | GRPO uses within-prompt sampled rewards without a separate learned critic. | Use TRL's implementation; do not reproduce the original training scale or claim its results transfer to this setup. |
| [Understanding R1-Zero-Like Training, §3 and Appendix G](https://arxiv.org/html/2503.20783v2) | Dr. GRPO removes response-length normalization and group reward standard-deviation normalization to address identified biases. | Explicit `dr_grpo` and unscaled rewards. Our nonzero KL coefficient is a design choice; the paper's reported configuration uses zero KL. |
| [Rubrics as Rewards](https://arxiv.org/html/2507.17746v1) | Explicit weighted criteria supply RL feedback beyond directly verifiable domains. Experiments concern scientific and medical tasks. | Reuse rubric decomposition; add an external mathematical correctness gate. The authors do not establish that rubrics prevent reward hacking. |
| [Learning Interestingness in Automated Mathematical Theory Formation](https://arxiv.org/html/2511.14778v1), [FERMAT code](https://github.com/trishullab/Fermat) | Formalizes concept discovery and theorem proving and learns interestingness heuristics using evolutionary search with abstraction. | Closest conceptual precedent for theory formation. Our natural-language explanations are not its formal symbolic discoveries and have weaker validity guarantees. |
| [Learning Formal Mathematics From Intrinsic Motivation](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/hash/4b8001fc75f0532827472ea5a16af9ca-Abstract-Conference.html) | Studies self-generated formal mathematical tasks and proofs. | Related motivation; we retain externally generated problems and do not claim autonomous discovery. |
| [Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.05685) | Evaluates LLM judges and documents biases including verbosity and position. | Require adversarial constructed calibration, independent-family evaluation, and length diagnostics. Cross-family judging does not guarantee independence or mathematical truth. |

passages.text: ## Grothendieck and attribution
passages.review: An intended procedure supplies no empirical effect estimate.

passages.text:
[Colin McLarty, *The Rising Sea: Grothendieck on simplicity and generality I*](https://ncatlab.org/nlab/files/McLartyRisingSea.pdf)
discusses building broad concepts until particular questions yield as consequences.
Its opening quotation cites *Récoltes et Semailles*, pages 552–553, and McLarty
states that its translations are his. The user-supplied nut/water passage is
included in the judge prompt with that attribution. The rubric is our research
operationalization: it cannot establish how Grothendieck would personally grade
a particular answer. Useful definitions, explicit assumptions, demonstrated
consequences, and economy are rewarded; abstraction without mathematical work is
not. Originality in the historical sense is unnecessary.
passages.review: Use the linked sources and stated evidence limits for each applicable claim.

passages.text:
The user also supplied a lecture paraphrase titled *Linear algebra and vector
analysis: Rising Sea*, commentary associated with
[3Blue1Brown's video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LKrwhjOI8Nc), and a
[social-media discussion](https://x.com/littmath/status/2109653733470572878).
These are distinct commentary sources, not direct Grothendieck quotations. The
[complete user-supplied passages](../docs/rising-sea-quotations.md) preserve all
wording with separate attributions and source-check notes. The lecture handout
and nLab entry were located; the supplied lecture version has small differences.
The video transcript and social-media wording have not been independently
authenticated. This commentary archive is not additional judge-prompt content
or empirical evidence for the training method.

passages.text: ## Reusable software and source audit
passages.review: An intended procedure supplies no empirical effect estimate.

passages.text:
* [Reasoning Gym](https://github.com/open-thought/reasoning-gym), Apache-2.0:
  reuse its generators, with recorded versions, parameters and seeds. Source
  inspection found `Random(seed + index)`; disjoint indices alone are insufficient
  if split seed intervals overlap. Canonical mathematical instance deduplication
  is required. Its native scores can be fractional or permissive, so our binary
  verifier does not reuse those scores as correctness labels.
* [Polynomial equations generator](https://github.com/open-thought/reasoning-gym/blob/main/reasoning_gym/algebra/polynomial_equations.py):
  generated answers use Python rounding, while its instruction says rounding
  down. Normalize the task instruction to nearest four decimal places; record
  the modification. Reject degenerate identities and verify reference roots.
* [Polynomial multiplication generator](https://github.com/open-thought/reasoning-gym/blob/main/reasoning_gym/algebra/polynomial_multiplication.py):
  monomials originate in a set. Fix `PYTHONHASHSEED`, archive complete manifests,
  and pin dependencies; seeds alone are not a sufficient reproducibility record.
* [Math-Verify](https://github.com/huggingface/Math-Verify), Apache-2.0 with
  component notices: use gold-first equivalence checks. Candidate expressions
  must pass a restricted arithmetic grammar before symbolic handling. Bound
  expression size and run verification in a resource-limited subprocess.
  Generated code is never executed.
* [TRL GRPO documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/trl/grpo_trainer): reuse
  trainer, loss and checkpoint machinery. Supply one composite reward so the
  correctness gate survives aggregation. The effective generation batch must
  be divisible by the number of completions per prompt. Explicitly configure
  loss, scaling, KL and lengths rather than depending on library defaults.
* [Unsloth Qwen3.5 guide](https://unsloth.ai/docs/models/qwen3.5/fine-tune):
  documents GRPO with `fast_inference=False`, Transformers v5, and BF16 LoRA.
  It cautions against Qwen3.5 4-bit QLoRA. Its fine-tuning memory table does not
  guarantee GRPO memory requirements. Local forward, backward and resumption
  measurements determine feasibility.
* [llama.cpp server](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/tree/master/tools/server),
  MIT: local GGUF serving and schema-constrained JSON. API compatibility does
  not mean remote API use. Bind to loopback only and pin its release/commit.

passages.text: ## Scientific validity and claim audit
passages.review: An intended procedure supplies no empirical effect estimate.

passages.text:
[Lones v4](https://arxiv.org/html/2108.02497v4) motivates separating development
from final testing and avoiding repeated test-driven selection.
[Lipton and Steinhardt](https://arxiv.org/html/1807.03341) motivate distinguishing
mechanistic explanation from speculation. The
[NeurIPS checklist](https://neurips.cc/public/guides/PaperChecklist) informs
limitations, reproducibility and uncertainty reporting.
passages.review: Use the linked sources and stated evidence limits for each applicable claim.

passages.text:
The primary metric is a proxy: correctness-weighted *Gemma-assessed* theory
quality. A verified final answer does not verify the explanation. Constructed
judge tests are not human preference data. Fresh generator instances cannot
exclude pretraining contamination of the mathematical ideas. Held-out task
families provide a narrower generalization test than new mathematical domains.
Transfer accuracy supplies an additional behavioral check, not a proof of
understanding or a latent-space mechanism. The exact combination has not been
found in the reviewed sources; this is not an exhaustive novelty claim.
passages.review: Use the linked sources and stated evidence limits for each applicable claim.

passages.text:
No source's published benchmark number is treated as a local measurement.
The later [judge-inference review](judge-inference-review.md) adds primary
studies of native reasoning and budget-dependent judging. Their settings do not
validate this project's novelty criterion; the local calibration gates remain.
passages.review: Use the linked sources and stated evidence limits for each applicable claim.

passages.text:
The pre-judgment novelty amendment adds a project-specific criterion; this is
an experimental design choice, not a metric established by a cited paper.
[FERMAT sections 3–5](https://arxiv.org/html/2511.14778v1) constructs definitions
and conjectures, checks them using formal backends, and evaluates recovery of
curated mathematical entities. Its comparisons show that simple novelty alone
is not a sufficient interestingness objective in that setting. We therefore
require justified utility and consequences, while acknowledging that our
natural-language judge supplies weaker validity evidence than formal checking.
The additional OOD suite uses existing [Reasoning Gym generators](https://github.com/open-thought/reasoning-gym)
and [SymPy matrix operations](https://docs.sympy.org/latest/modules/matrices/matrices.html)
and [modular inverses](https://docs.sympy.org/latest/modules/core.html#sympy.core.intfunc.mod_inverse).
These held-out families do not establish out-of-pretraining generalization.
No code from papers is copied where an existing library implements the method.
Runtime and task-source compatibility will be checked against the locked release,
with deviations documented before comparative results.

passages.text: ## A distinct route: verified mathematical construction
passages.review: An intended procedure supplies no empirical effect estimate.

passages.text:
[ALPS, sections 3–4 and appendices](https://arxiv.org/html/2608.15979v1) asks for
a triviality proof or a finite presentation of a nontrivial model of an
equational law. Its construction channel checks both entailment of the law and
satisfiability with distinct elements, using complete prover saturation;
triviality is checked through Lean. This motivates checking that proposed
objects satisfy their specification without becoming degenerate. It does not
validate our natural-language score or establish historical originality of a
successful construction. Appendix H reports repeated solver passes, so the
headline counts should not be treated as a matched causal comparison of prompt
conditions. The full paper and appendices were reviewed. No code, prompts or
data are imported; adopting this different task and verification interface
would require a separate experiment. The current locked OOD suite is unchanged.

Wrong or malformed answer: zero. Correct answer: one. Supported, useful theory can add up to one half. Constructive novelty has 20% of rubric weight: new objects, definitions, invariants, frameworks and distant connections must be justified and useful relative to documented conventional approaches. The other criteria assess structure, generality, derivation, reuse and conceptual economy. False theory, cosmetic renaming and unsupported originality claims earn no theory bonus.


Novelty is reference-relative. The additional OOD suite tests graph connectivity, polygon geometry, matrix rank and modular inverses held out from project training. Neither measure establishes historical discovery or absence from model pretraining.

Qualification thresholds and failed historical results stay fixed; a separate experiment tests whether the imperfect reward is useful for learning.



The rising-sea philosophy motivates building definitions and general principles until the original problem becomes a consequence. This rubric is a research interpretation of Grothendieck, not a claim to reproduce his personal judgments.

passages.text: Any divisor of 2n and 3n divides their difference n, and every divisor of n divides both. Thus gcd(2n,3n)=n for positive n. The same argument gives gcd(a,b)=gcd(a,b-a), the invariant of Euclid's algorithm.

passages.text: View I(a,b)={ua+vb: u,v integers} as the lattice of reachable displacements on an integer line. It is closed under addition and negation. Let d be its least positive element for nonzero positive a,b. Dividing any t in I by d leaves a remainder in I smaller than d, hence zero. Therefore I=dZ. Both a,b are multiples of d; every common divisor divides every ua+vb, so d is their gcd. This turns gcd into the spacing of a reachable lattice. For a=2n,b=3n, every displacement is a multiple of n and n=3n-2n is reachable, so I=nZ. Further, ua+vb=t has an integer solution exactly when d divides t; with these step sizes n is reachable and n+1 is not for n>1. The construction requires integer signed moves; nonnegative moves do not form a subgroup.

passages.text: Represent exact recurring events by subgroups aZ,bZ of integer time. Their intersection is a subgroup; if l is its least positive element, division with remainder shows every member is a multiple of l. Hence aZ intersect bZ=lZ and l=lcm(a,b). For 2n and 3n this is 6nZ, since t=n*k must have 6 dividing k. For events with phases r,s the schedules are cosets r+aZ and s+bZ. If a common time t0 exists, subtracting t0 shows their entire intersection is t0+lZ. Thus a single coincidence determines all future coincidences. For phases r=s=n with periods 2n,3n, common times are n+6nZ. Arbitrary phases may give an empty intersection: even times and odd times with period 2 never coincide.

passages.text: Distributivity in a commutative ring gives (x+n)(x-n)=x*x-x*n+n*x-n*n =x**2-n**2. The general identity (a+b)(a-b)=a**2-b**2 also computes (m+1)(m-1)=m**2-1. Noncommuting products retain a cross-term commutator.

passages.text: Use the quadratic algebra A=R[x][e]/(e**2-1): each element has unique form a+b*e, with a,b in R[x]. Conjugation a+b*e -> a-b*e preserves products, so the scalar norm N(a+b*e)=a**2-b**2 is multiplicative. Indeed N(uv)=uv*conj(u)*conj(v)=N(u)*N(v) by commutativity. Setting u=x+n*e gives N(u)=x**2-n**2, equal to (x+n)(x-n) by evaluation at e=1 and e=-1. This yields the reusable composition law (a**2-b**2)(c**2-d**2) =(a*c+b*d)**2-(a*d+b*c)**2, by multiplying the two pairs. The algebra has zero divisors: (1+e)(1-e)=0 although both factors are nonzero; it is not a field.

passages.text: For an even-sided fair die, half the faces are even and half odd. Independence gives P(even sum)=P(even,even)+P(odd,odd)=1/4+1/4=1/2. More generally, independent dice with even-face probabilities p,q give p*q+(1-p)*(1-q).

passages.text: Encode parity by the character chi(k)=(-1)**k of the additive integers into {1,-1}. Its law chi(a+b)=chi(a)*chi(b) changes addition into multiplication. The even indicator is (1+chi(k))/2. Independence therefore gives P(X+Y even)=(1+E[chi(X)]*E[chi(Y)])/2. Each even-sided fair die has equally many signs, so each expectation is zero and the answer is 1/2. For any number of independent integer-valued variables, the same argument gives even-sum probability (1+product_i E[chi(X_i)])/2; one parity-balanced summand suffices. Independence matters: for Y=X with X uniform on {1,2}, each expectation is zero but X+Y is always even. This character transform is a reusable bridge from probability convolution to multiplicative statistics.

passages.text: Grothendieck's rising-sea metaphor motivates building structures until a specific question becomes a consequence. McLarty's account supplies the historical attribution [1]. We combine GRPO [2], Dr. GRPO normalization [3], and rubric rewards [4]. FERMAT [5] studies symbolic theory formation; this study instead scores natural-language explanations. The contribution is a correctness-gated experimental protocol and reusable environment, not a new optimizer.

passages.text: Tasks come from pinned Reasoning Gym generators [6]. Training families are GCD, LCM, polynomial multiplication and dice probabilities. Semantic deduplication separates train, development, fresh, harder and unseen-family evaluation. One terminal final-answer field is checked by restricted arithmetic and Math-Verify [7]. Correctness C multiplies the entire reward: R=C(1+0.5T). Theory T is a six-criterion rubric score gated by supported validity. Constructive novelty receives 20% weight, judged relative to published conventional approaches. New objects, definitions, invariants, frameworks and distant mathematical connections earn that credit only when justified and useful. Historical originality and pretraining distribution are not inferred. Supporting excerpts are required. The two-call protocol separated conceptual analysis from overall validity and quality. Its historical fallback used eight specialist roles. That protocol derived novelty from explicit addition, application and consequence findings, and withholds novelty unless supported theory is declared beyond-reference with an excerpt identifying a concrete addition. Brief valid connections can earn one novelty point without a further worked use; developed mathematics can earn up to four. A reference argument establishing a connection is not itself a further application. Raw stage findings are retained; code derives combined scores and any substantive objection vetoes the bonus. Checklist-based judging [14] and decomposition [15] motivate auditable prerequisites; the checks do not certify mathematical entailment. Final-answer verification does not certify surrounding proofs.

passages.text:
Preregistered local Qwen/Gemma research on correctness-gated theory-building
rewards, including valid conceptual novelty relative to fixed reference approaches.
This repository publishes deterministic Reasoning Gym and SymPy-backed manifests,
provenance, model/runtime locks, protocol, code and generated research reports.
Model-generated results are pending unless explicitly recorded in saved results.
Development evidence includes failed Gemma and bounded-reasoning Qwen novelty
calibrations, as well as interrupted attempts. No comparative improvement is
established. Qualification-study training and locked audits remain blocked; the full negative
results and their limitations are preserved in `reports/experiments/`.
The v5 attempt stopped on repeated reference/score contradictions; v6 executed
an explicit eligibility gate and was interrupted after the user clarified the
intended scoring construct. Rubric v7 permits modest credit for brief valid
connections without a further worked use, with higher credit for developed
frameworks. Raw and credited scores, caps and reasons remain separate. Weights
remain fixed; changed calibration contrasts now distinguish brief connections
from zero-novelty reference controls. The fresh v7 attempt failed its fixed
futility gate: developed frameworks ranked higher, but the control-credit
conditions failed. False-theory suppression was not reached. The generated
reports separate those checks and preserve every raw opinion.
Reference version v3 subsequently clarifies the commutative-polynomial and
ordinary biased-probability baselines. The rubric, case hashes and thresholds
remained fixed. The fresh trial also failed: probability control credit improved,
but brief-connection credit and a framework/control ranking still disagreed with
the constructed expectations. A routine reference excerpt was incorrectly used
as evidence of an additional connection's application. Exact substring checks
cannot certify that semantic relationship. The negative result is preserved in
`reports/experiments/qwen-v7-reference-scope-learnings.md`; remaining calibration,
audits and qualification-study training stay blocked.

a brief valid commutator connection, but overcredited routine GCD/LCM mathematics

gate. False mathematical objections vetoed valid frameworks and the brief
commutator connection. Full evidence, selected exact mathematical checks and

connection credit, weights, thresholds and saved failures. Explicit experiment

retaining the same scoring rubric and unqualified interpretation. Both the

The repaired development pilot subsequently completed saving and resumption,
advanced the task position and changed adapter parameters. Its discarded updates
are execution evidence only. The generated pilot report and boundary records
retain timings, reward components, retries and checkpoint state. Ordinary baseline
generation was stopped and its prompted queue cancelled when the user prioritized
the smaller GPU experiment. Partial outputs and the larger configuration are
preserved. Comparative training and scored held-out evaluation remain pending.
